subject: Vantage AI — sudden latency surge, elevated 5xx/429; coordinating customer comms
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@vantageai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@vantageai.com
Date: 2027-04-18T08:15:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden latency spike + 5xx/429s — immediate help needed

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp jump in request latencies (~2-3x) at ~07:50 UTC and a corresponding rise in 5xx/429s across multiple model routes. This is impacting our inference traffic for the recommendation feature; user-facing errors are increasing.

Attached is a small log snippet from our side and a short timeline. Can Redwood confirm whether this is platform-side or something from our request patterns? We are seeing client retries which may be amplifying the problem.

We’d like an initial ETA and whether you recommend any immediate mitigations we can do on our end (e.g., backoff, temporary throttling).

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Director of Platform, Vantage AI

Attachment: vantage_error_log_snippet.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:23:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden latency spike + 5xx/429s — immediate help needed

Folks — forwarding Vantage's alert. Triage notes below. Please prioritize.

Observed: platform-side tail latency increase correlated with sudden spike in circuit fallback to lower-capacity backends. We are seeing two simultaneous contributors: (1) KV-cache invalidation event caused cache miss amplification for long-prefix requests, (2) an emergent retry storm from a subset of clients at Vantage that is increasing QPS beyond provisioned pooling for some pinned CPUs. Both factors together pushed certain routes into queueing and 429 responses.

Immediate asks:
- Sean: can you spin up an emergency pool for the affected routes (temp capacity + remove strict pinning) and enable the adaptive batching guardrail?
- Karthik: check the routing policy — roll traffic to compatible model-variants in eu-west fallback lanes and enable short-circuit responses for known circuit-breaker patterns.
- Marissa: prepare a short customer-facing update and a statuspage draft.

I’ll coordinate with Vantage's Ops. Attaching quick mitigation playbook.

— Mina
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation_playbook.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden latency spike + 5xx/429s — immediate help needed

On 18 Apr 2027 08:23, Mina Haddad wrote:
> Immediate asks:
> - Sean: can you spin up an emergency pool for the affected routes (temp capacity + remove strict pinning) and enable the adaptive batching guardrail?

Done. I’ve:
- provisioned two emergency GPU pods in us-central and removed strict CPU pinning for the routes: "recommendation-predict" and "rec-embed-v2" (traffic is being spread across the new pool).
- enabled adaptive batching cap at 120ms to avoid excessive queueing.
- implemented a short-lived token-bucket on the affected API keys to smooth bursts.

Early telemetry shows error rates decreasing for the next 5 minutes; still monitoring. I also kicked a fast rollback of a recent kernel selection tweak that increased tail latency for long-seq runs.

Will update in 15m with more stable numbers.

— Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@vantageai.com>, ops@vantageai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spike + 5xx/429s — immediate help needed

Emily — quick interim update from Redwood:

Thanks for the logs. We see a combination of cache invalidation and amplified retry traffic as the root contributors. Immediate mitigations we've applied:
- Emergency capacity added (us-central) and strict CPU pinning relaxed.
- Adaptive batching and an interim token-bucket limiter on your bursty API keys to blunt the retry storm.
- Rolled back a recent kernel selection change that elevated tail latency on long-seq runs.

ETA: we expect error rates to fall to baseline within 30–45 minutes if the client retry rate subsides. Recommended customer action for fastest recovery: temporarily implement exponential backoff (backoff jitter suggested) or reduce client-side retry attempts for the next 1 hour. We can also apply a temporary per-key throttle at your direction — let us know which API keys you want capped.

Status page: we’ll publish an incident note within the hour (draft attached) and link to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/7891.

I’ll follow up shortly with a more detailed timeline and next steps.

— Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: statuspage_draft.md

From: David Nguyen <david.nguyen@vantageai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@vantageai.com>, ops@vantageai.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spike + 5xx/429s — immediate help needed

Thanks for the rapid response. We pushed a temporary client-side backoff (backoff multiplier x2, max retries=2) and disabled a bursty retry loop in our pool. We’ll share metrics in ~20 minutes.

Question: can Redwood apply a 5–10% traffic shadow to the eu-west fallback lane instead of hard routing so we can validate correctness without cutting capacity in us? Prefer not to risk model mismatch for users.

— David Nguyen
SRE, Vantage AI

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T13:42:00Z
Subject: Executive summary: Vantage AI incident (resolved for now) — 5xx/429 spike, root cause, and follow-ups

Team — brief exec summary for leadership and ops:

What happened:
- At ~07:50 UTC we observed a sudden latency surge on customer-facing recommendation routes, with elevated 5xx and 429 responses.
- Root contributors: a transient KV-cache invalidation that created a large number of cache misses, a concurrently triggered client retry storm from Vantage, and a recent kernel selection rollback that impacted tail latency for long sequences.

What we did (timeline highlights):
- 08:23: triage + mitigation plan (Mina).
- 08:38: emergency capacity + adaptive batching + token-bucket smoothing (Sean).
- 08:55: customer notified; recommended client-side backoff and temporary throttles.
- 09:05–09:30: Vantage applied client mitigations; error rates dropped to near baseline.

Status: customer-facing error rates are reduced and user impact is substantially mitigated. We will keep the emergency pools for the next 6 hours and then scale down if telemetry remains stable.

Action items / follow-ups (owners):
- Post-incident RCA writeup with timeline and code refs (Marissa).
- Permanent guardrail: KV-cache invalidation detection + automated cache-warming (Karthik).
- Review kernel selection rollout process and add staged canary metrics for long-seq latency (Sean).
- Coordinate final customer postmortem and share with Vantage execs (Mina / Marissa).

I’ve attached the mitigation playbook and statuspage draft for review. Recommend sharing a short customer postmortem by EOD and scheduling a 1:1 postmortem review with Vantage next week.

— Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf, statuspage_draft.md
